In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, the fishery resource of Lake Tana was governed by a set of informal rules, which are embedded in the social norms of the local people.
, there were no legally and socially binding rules and institutions at the user level to govern fishery sector in Lake Tana.

, there is a need for a comprehensive and integrated fishery management plan, which should include the following components: 1) a comprehensive and detailed fishery resource assessment and management plan, 2) a fisher's rights and responsibilities and 3) a fishery management and enforcement plan.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, the fishery sector of Lake Tana is in a state of transition, from traditional fishery to a modernized fishery, and the fishery sector is in a state where it is in need of a new set of rules and institutions that are capable of managing the sector in a more sustainable manner.
, the governance of Lake Tane fishery is in the process of being developed.
there were no formal rules that govern fishery resource management at the user level.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there are no formal institutions that are responsible to manage and govern the fishery resource in the study area and the fishery sector is under the responsibility of Bureau of Agriculture, which is the main agency responsible to manage and develop the agriculture sector.
the fishery sector is not only the responsibility of the government but it is the collective responsibility of the community, government and private stakeholders.
, there is a need to strengthen the existing fishery management institutions and develop new institutions at user level to ensure the sustainability and governance of the fishery sector.
